I was a treeplanter for a couple years. At the end of one summer, I had still a couple weeks left and my contract ended, so I jumped on the bandwagon of another contract. The foreman was desperate for experienced treeplanters so his all-newbies crew could get some experience watching someone getting the job done. My extractor had a long handle (think of shovels with short handle versus long hande).

The newbies had no idea I was experienced. The betters among them boasted how much money they were doing up front when they saw me for the first time. On the first day I planted more than twice what their best guy was doing. I was good, but not a star. Just good. But they were really, really just newbies.

They tough I had given it all, and that I would never do that much again. For them, it was record-breaking; for me it was the minimum I would do on any given day. So days passed and I kept planting what was, for them, an insane amount of trees. They were baffled. Some of them, looking at my long-handled extractor, though it kinda looked like a spear, which is pronounced "lance" in french (we all spoke in french). They started to call me "Lancelot" behind my back, then to my face. It grew on me. I kept the name, adding another "a" so I wouldn't always have to add a number after it.

Amare - a Latin verb meaning "to love" and often viewed as a pure, altruistic love different from lust or even romance. More like the love of truth or the kindness of a good person. In the general conjugation it can also mean the object or subject of these feelings. Latin plays fast-and-loose with their grammatical rules that way.

Damear - a Greek verb from the king Dameus, who was a cruel and despotic tyrant. His name became synonymous with "to control or subdue, for the purpose of destroying." Fun fact: The name Damien is also derived from the same root.

-eus - makes it an action verb, much like "er" in english. Adding er to Destroy makes Destroyer, one who destroys.

So we fudge a little bit of the conjugations and ignore the Latin/Greek conflict to get AMAre + DAMear + EUS with a pronunciation "AH-muh-DAY-mee-us"

AMADAMEUS, one who subdues and controls that which he loves - for the ultimate purpose of destroying it.
